paragraphs.text: In this chapter are set forth rationes et ritus, the laws and rites that were to be observed by prince and people in offering their sacrifices. It is the manner of performance that maketh or marreth any duty. There may be malum opus in bona materia, ill work in a good matter.
paragraphs.anchor: Thus saith the Lord God.

paragraphs.text: Of the priests’ court.
paragraphs.anchor: The gate of the inner court.

paragraphs.text: That pointeth to Christ, the day spring from on high, the Sun of righteousness, who shineth sweetly upon such as rightly sanctify the Sabbath, and shall much more when they come to rest with him in heaven.
paragraphs.anchor: That looketh toward the east.

paragraphs.text: Six days shalt thou labour and do all thy work. Neither doth this hinder holiness, as the abbey lubbers pretend, but further it: (1.) By preventing temptation; (2.) By nourishing experience of God’s bounty and providence; (3.) By filling the heart with objects of heavenly thoughts; (4.) By stirring up to prayer and praise for each day’s mercies.
paragraphs.anchor: Shall be shut the six working days.

paragraphs.text: That the people may see Christ in the glass of the ceremonies, and call upon his name. We under the gospel have a clearer light and free access, on Lord’s days especially, and other times of holy meetings.
paragraphs.anchor: But on the Sabbath it shall be opened.

paragraphs.text: Waiting at the posts of the gates of wisdom. {Pro 8:34} Constantine the Great stood up constantly at the time of God’s public worship for honour sake. So did our Edward VI.
paragraphs.anchor: And shall stand by the post of the gate.

paragraphs.text: And the people come in, {Eze 46:3} whose souls are as precious to God as his.
paragraphs.anchor: Then he shall go forth.

paragraphs.text: The gate is open till the evening; be ready therefore. When the bridegroom is once gone in, the gate is shut, and fools excluded. {Mat 25:10-12}
paragraphs.anchor: But the gate shall not be shut until the evening.

paragraphs.text: The meanest of his subjects, if faithful, may have as near access to God as himself.
paragraphs.anchor: Likewise the people of the land.

paragraphs.text: This was a larger sacrifice than Moses had appointed {Num 28:9} - Christians have more cause than Jews had to sanctify the Sabbath - as that for the new moons {Eze 46:6} was lesser. See Num 28:11. Hereby it appeareth that God was about to abrogate the Mosaical worship, and the Levitical priesthood: Lex enim posterior derogat priori. This the Jewish doctors would fain say something to, but cannot tell what. The wit of these miscreants, reprobate concerning the faith, will better serve them to devise a thousand shifts to elude the truth, than their obstinace will suffer them once to yield and acknowledge it.
paragraphs.anchor: Six lambs without blemish.

paragraphs.text: Heb., The gift of his hand. Some render it, According as it shall be given unto his hand - i.e., as God shall put into his heart to give; and here he is not tied, as in the law, to such a proportion, but left to his Christian liberty.
paragraphs.anchor: As he shall be able to give.

paragraphs.text: Which pointed them to the coming of Christ, by whom all things are become new.
paragraphs.anchor: And in the day of the new moon.

paragraphs.text: It was wont to be two. See on Eze 46:4.
paragraphs.anchor: It shall be a young bullock.

paragraphs.text: To signify, saith Rabanus, that as it is necessary for us to keep the Sabbath; so it is likewise that we rely upon Christ for expiation as of our week days’ sins, so also of those that we fall into even on that holy day.
paragraphs.anchor: And six lambs and a ram.

paragraphs.text: This was to shadow out, saith Polanus, the communion of the saints with Christ, and that Christ offereth and presenteth his Church with himself and in himself to God the Father.
paragraphs.anchor: An ephah for a bullock.

paragraphs.text: i.e., As he is able and willing, for God straineth upon none.
paragraphs.anchor: According as his hand shall attain unto

paragraphs.text: This was the prince’s privilege, that, as likewise the priests, he might go in and go out at the same east gate. It is fit that the word and sword should hold together, and that magistrates and ministers should be singular in holiness.
paragraphs.anchor: He shall go in by the way of the porch.

paragraphs.text: For more easy passage sake, in such a multitude of people. But withal to teach us many things; as (1.) Not to turn our backs upon the holy ordinances; {a} (2.) To "make straight paths for our feet"; {Heb 12:13} not looking back with Lot’s wife; {Luk 17:32} not longing for the onions of Egypt, as those rebels in the wilderness, but advancing forward with St Paul, {Php 3:13-14} looking forthright, {Pro 4:25} having our eye upon the mark, and making daily progress toward perfection; (3.) That our memories are frail, and here we shall meet with many things that will withdraw us from thinking upon God; (4.) That our life is but short; a very passage from one gate to another: where to go back - i.e., to add anything to our lives - it is not granted, since our time is limited, {Job 14:3 Act 17:26} and we are all hastening to our long home. {Ecc 12:5} One being asked what life was? made an answer answerless; for he presently went his way.
paragraphs.anchor: Shall go out the way of the south gate.

paragraphs.text: {a} The Jews at this day depart out of the synagogue with their faces still toward the ark, like crabs going backward.

For example sake, Vita Principis censura est, and to see that all things be rightly carried in God’s service. And although the prince hath many weighty occasions, yet he is to be at the public assemblies with the first, and to stay till the last.
paragraphs.anchor: And the prince in the midst of them, &c.

paragraphs.text: A whole ephah, and a whole hin, whereas in the Mosaical service there was required but a certain part only of either; because the Jewish Church was but of a part of mankind, but the Church Christian is universal. {a}
paragraphs.anchor: An ephah to a bullock, and a hin of oil.

paragraphs.text: {a} Polan.

A voluntary burnt offering … one shall then open him the gate, &c.] Here is warrant for our week day lectures, a voluntary service well accepted; provided that afterwards one shut the gate, and men return to their honest labours.

God must be served daily and duly, not on the Sabbath day only. See Psa 72:15. The Papists are at their mass every morning, and they bind much upon this text for it. They have a proverb also, Mass and meat hindereth no man’s thrift.
paragraphs.anchor: Thou shalt daily prepare a burnt offering.

paragraphs.text: This is also different from the Levitical ordinance, {Num 15:3-12; Num 28:3-5 Exo 29:40} though R. Solomon here extremely troubleth himself, but to no purpose, to reconcile them.
paragraphs.anchor: The sixth part of an ephah.

paragraphs.text: Understand it of every evening also. {as Exo 29:38}
paragraphs.anchor: Every morning.

paragraphs.text: As Jehoshaphat did cities to every one of his sons; though they long enjoyed them not, through the barbarous cruelty of their elder brother Jehoram. Christ, the Church’s king, giveth all his children gifts of great price; such as the world can neither give nor take from them, "spiritual blessings in heavenly" things and "places"; {Eph 1:3} yea, he bestoweth himself upon them, and is therefore called "The gift," {Joh 4:10} and "The benefit." {1Ti 6:2}
paragraphs.anchor: If the prince give a gift unto any of his sons.

paragraphs.text: As Alexander the Great, who, going to subdue a great part of the habitable world, gave away to his servants almost all he had, and when one of his officers asked him what he would leave for himself? he said, Hope. Messiah the prince, besides his choicest gifts ( Dona throni) to his dear children, giveth gifts unto men, even to the rebellious also; {Psa 68:18} these are common gifts ( Dona scabelli), temporal favours, external privileges. See Mat 7:22-23; Mat 25:14-30 Luk 19:12-27, &c. But as "the servant abideth not in the house for ever," as the son doth; {Joh 8:35} so these gifts to servants, but for the behoof and benefit of his sons, are but till the year of liberty, or jubilee, till the last day at utmost. {Lev 25:10} Then shall the wicked give a dreadful account of all, with the whole world flaming about their ears.
paragraphs.anchor: But if he give a gift of his inheritance to one of his servants.

paragraphs.text: Ill accidents attend such princes, as affecting to be absolute in power, will be too resolute in will, or dissolute in life; oppressing their subjects to enrich their servants and parasites.
paragraphs.anchor: To thrust them out of their possession.

paragraphs.text: Here he returneth again to things sacred - viz., to show where the priests should boil and bake.
paragraphs.anchor: Afterward he brought me.

paragraphs.text: These holy cells or chambers are particular Christian churches, committed to the care of Christ’s faithful ministers {a} {Act 20:28 1Pe 5:2}
paragraphs.anchor: Into the holy chambers of the priests.

paragraphs.text: {a} Polan.

i.e., The ministers shall indite or boil good matters in their hearts for the use of the people, and then their tongues shall be as the pen of a ready writer. {Psa 45:1} They shall not feed their hearers with crude and indigested stuff, but such as is well boiled and baked with the fire of the Holy Spirit, kindled on the hearth of their own hearts; that from the heart they may speak to the heart.
paragraphs.anchor: Where they shall bake the meat offering

paragraphs.text: As in promiscuous communions, where all are pell-mell admitted.
paragraphs.anchor: To sanctify the people.

paragraphs.text: And buildings in every of them for the same purpose round about. {Eze 46:22} These served, saith Jerome, to set forth the four parts of the world, out of all which the Church is gathered by ministers, &c. It served also, saith another, to show that in God’s house, which is his Church, there shall always be provision both for his ministers and people. Those that have but from hand to mouth have their bread hot, as it were, from God’s hand, which is best of all.
paragraphs.anchor: In every corner of the court there was a court.

paragraphs.text: Or made with chimneys. Caminata, vaporaria. See on Eze 46:21.
paragraphs.anchor: Courts joined.

paragraphs.text: Such as the ancients called popinas.
paragraphs.anchor: With boiling places.

paragraphs.text: “ Nolo ego Florus esse,
Latitare per popinas. ”{ a}
“I do not wish to be Florus,
to hide in the kitchens.”
{a} Adrian. Imp.
Of God’s cooks, who dress spiritual food for the use of his people. See Eze 46:20.
paragraphs.anchor: These are the places of them that boil.
